WE're in the redfish namespace, there's no reason to specify redfish::.


This is done in several places, please fix all of them.
remvoed the code.

removed the code.

same here.

There are lots of places where auto is misused, please fix all of them
removed the code.
This is a request copy?
Acknowledged
DOesn't appear fixed?
this is old patch. we dont have this code in the new patch.
Should we pass in the request object at all here?  Is there any use that's correct?
We pass the sub_request object here. In contains the patch payload. I think your comment was first patchset which is been changed.
This param shouldn't be ignored, right?  Otherwise this code will work for any manager
Since its validated in main handler before calling OEM, its optional to check here again.
Done
Need more than one unit test here.
Sure. will update.
I have added all the IT test cases ran on qemu daytonax image. Please review if anything else need to be added. I will push another MR to enhance the UT coverage.
Considering daytonax doesn't support the URIs you've changed (which are entity-manager), that doesn't seem like enough of a test.
when you load daytonax all Oem/OpenBMC/Fan data shows up and it allows PATCH of new configuration which gets reflected in the backend.
What did you actually test here?  We need to test something functional and visible to a user.  "handlers are invoked" isn't a proper test.
sure will update.
Acknowledged
Can we make this an explicit object please that has no methods?  If we intend that this is how we'll do OEM schemas, then we should enforce it at some level.

I am assuming by explicit you mean remove the optional one right ?. If we remove optional and patch does not contain the OEM i think the readJsonPatch would expect the OEM to be present as mandatory element right ?

No, I mean that we need an object that isn't object_t.  If the oem schemas don't parse, the next line needs to return an error and run no handlers.  Right now you have to start executing handlers before you know if there's an error.
I have kept the payload parsing unchanged for now. Its main handler which will parse the schema of OEM and return if there are errors.
For every patch handler, it seems like this (which is a copy) would always be the first handler.  Should we instead just pass in the object itself?

I had this passing via reference but later had to change it to copy because the readJsonObject would except a const reference payload coming from const SubRequest& req. This is just fragment of the payload OEM handler is interested in which is copied. Not the whole patch payload or not the whole OEM payload which is passed by the main router.
*readJsonObject expects a non-const reference.
So make it non const?  We shouldn't be copying the payload.
I have already tried that but code fails in lot many other places. I think I can push another MR separately for this.
current this is not required.
As written, errors will now be incorrect if the value fails to parse.
OEM schema parsing will be still done by the main handler if there are errors we will not call any of the sub handlers.
Done
This function is called out by name as banned.
Acknowledged
Does this need to be more specific than just whether it's empty?
I think its ok here to check for just being empty. SubRequest construction ensures it's not empty and its type is already object.
